findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Employees were observed washing hands then using their newly-clean hands to turn off the faucet or dispense paper towels from the wall-mounted dispenser. CORRECTED- Inspector provided education. Employees need to use a paper towel or other barrier when dispensing paper towels and when turning off the faucet to prevent recontaminating their hands. Review handwashing procedures with all employees.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Raw shell eggs were eobserved stored on the top shelf of the short prep cooler, above squeeze-bottles of sauces and other ready-to-eat foods. Upon further discussion, PIC stated that the eggs are employee personal foods, not for service. CORRECTED- PIC designated the right-most door of the long prep cooler for storage of personal foods. The carton of eggs was moved to be stored away from foods for service. Ensure foods are stored to prevent potential cross contamination during storage.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Chlorine sanitizer in the 3 compartment sink was observed at 10ppm. CORRECTED- Inspector alerted the PIC, who added more chlorine to the sanitizer solution. Sanitizer was then observed at 50ppm Cl. Use test strips to verify sanitizer solution concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a concentration of 50-200ppm. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Six individual portions of mac & cheese were observed without dates in the 3 door cooler. CORRECTED- PIC labeled the portions with the date their original package was opened. Ensure all ready-to-eat TCS foods are labeled with the date they were opened, and used or discarded within 7 days after.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: Ambient thermometers were not observed in the 3 door cooler or in the long prep cooler. Provide ambient air thermometers for all cold holding units.
findings.citation_text: 4-203.12 Temperature Measuring Devices, Ambient Air and Water. (A) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled in Celsius or dually scaled in Celsius and Fahrenheit shall be designed to be easily readable and accurate to ±1.5°C in the intended range of use. (B) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±3°F in the intended range of use. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: The end of the shelving holding Cajun seasoning is unfinished and needs to be sealed. Paint or otherwise seal the bare end of the shelf.
findings.citation_text: 4-201.11 Equipment and Utensils. EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be designed and constructed to be durable and to retain their characteristic qualities under normal use conditions. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
1) Frost accumulation was observed on the interior of the right chest freezer. Defrost the freezer regularly to eliminate frost accumulation and maintain the interior of the freezer smooth and easily cleanable.
2) Price tag stickers were observed on metal lids in the prep coolers. Clean lids to remove stickers.
3) Food debris was observed on the interior of the microwave. CORRECTED- PIC discussed with an employee, who cleaned the inside of the microwave.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: The following physical facilities items are in need of attention: 
1) An electrical outlet on the cookline is askew and does not cover the area cut out of the wall. See that outlets fit properly on the walls. 
2) Seal the handsink to the wall. The handsink, while secured to the wall, is not firmly in place and has some give which may make sealing it to the wall difficult.
3) Cracked caulking is observed at the bathroom handsink. Recaulk to eliminate the cracks.
4) Ceiling tiles in bathroom are acoustic and should be vinyl coated - replace tiles
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: PIC is not a certified food protection manager. Ensure sufficient CFMs are on staff to cover all shifts of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Facility does not have a written policy for clean up of vomit/diarrhea. CORRECTED- Inspector provided a vomit/diarrhea clean up policy. Keep available for review in case it is needed and ensure supplies are available.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: No soap was available at the prep area handwashing sink. CORRECTED- PIC found soap within the facility to provide at the handwashing sink. Ensure soap is always available.
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Paper towels were not available at the kitchen handwashing sink. CORRECTED- PIC provided paper towels. Ensure paper towels are always available at all handwashing sinks.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Raw shell eggs observed stored above milk and cheese in the customer reach in cooler. CORRECTED- Reviewed proper storage order. PIC moved eggs to the lowest shelf.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce.  [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Packages of hot dogs were observed past their manufacturer use-by date of 11/4/24. CORRECTED- Hot dogs were voluntarily discarded. Ensure foods are sold or discarded before their expiration dates.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: Facility does not have any Cl (bleach) available to make a sanitizer solution. CORRECTED- PIC had someone bring bleach to the facility. Ensure sanitizer is available during all times of food prep and service.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11 (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: Drywall around the back door (behind the meat chest freezer) is heavily damaged resulting in holes and areas which are not smooth, non-absorbent and/or easily cleanable. The drywall was must be sealed and holes filled to create smooth, easily cleanable surfaces.
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. [C]
